title: Normal schemes with Noetherian underlying space have open integral components
statement: Let $Z$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] whose underlying topological space is Noetherian, meaning that every descending chain of closed subsets stabilizes. Suppose $Z$ is normal: for every $z\in Z$, the local ring $\mathcal O_{Z,z}$ is an integral domain integrally closed in its fraction field [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring]. Then $Z$ has finitely many irreducible components [def-weil-irreducible-components]; they are pairwise disjoint open and closed subsets, and with their open subscheme structures they are normal integral schemes [def-pc-integral-scheme]. The empty scheme is allowed, with zero components. No local Noetherian condition on the structure sheaf is assumed.

source.place: Tag 0357, lemma-normal-locally-finite-nr-irreducibles; the finiteness condition for every quasi-compact open follows from Tag 0052, topology.tex, lemma-Noetherian (1)--(2).

proof.text: Every open subset $U\subseteq Z$ is topologically Noetherian: write a descending sequence of relatively closed subsets as $F_n=U\cap H_n$ with $H_n$ closed in $Z$, replace $H_n$ by $H_1\cap\cdots\cap H_n$, and use stabilization in $Z$. The resulting traces are still $F_n$. This uses only the given descending-chain condition, not Noetherianness of any ring.

Apply [lem-sc-noetherian-finite-irreducible-components] to $|Z|$ and to the underlying space of each affine open $U$. Thus both have finitely many irreducible components. Write $U=\operatorname{Spec}R$, with $R=\mathcal O_Z(U)$, using [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-spec-points]. By [lem-weil-pbc-spec-irreducible-components-minimal-primes] these affine components are exactly $V(\mathfrak q)$ for minimal primes $\mathfrak q$ of $R$. Distinct minimal primes give distinct subsets: $\mathfrak q\in V(\mathfrak q)$, and equality of two such sets gives both inclusions of their primes. Therefore $R$ has finitely many minimal primes.

Every local ring of $Z$ is a domain, hence is reduced: $a^n=0$ in a domain implies $a=0$. The equivalence in [def-pc-reduced-scheme] therefore gives that every section ring, in particular $R=\mathcal O_Z(U)$, is reduced. For each prime $\mathfrak p$ of $R$, [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-stalk-localization] identifies $R_{\mathfrak p}$ with $\mathcal O_{Z,x}$ at the corresponding point $x\in U$. It is a normal domain by hypothesis. Thus $R$ is a normal ring in precisely the prime-localization sense of [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring].

source.place: Tags 01J0/01J1, definition-reduced and lemma-reduced; Tag 01HV, lemma-spec-sheaves (6)

proof.text: The affine section ring $R$ is now reduced, normal, and has finitely many minimal primes. Apply implication (1) to (3) of [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-normal-iff-integrally-closed-total-fractions] to obtain $R\simeq\prod_{i=1}^n A_i$ with each $A_i$ a normal domain. These are exactly the hypotheses of that node; no ring-theoretic Noetherian hypothesis occurs. The zero ring is the empty product.

source.place: Tag 030C, lemma-characterize-reduced-ring-normal, (1) implies (3); used in properties.tex Tag 0357, affine case

proof.text: Here is the elementary component calculation for this product. Let $e_i$ be the coordinate idempotents, so $e_i e_j=0$ for $i\ne j$ and $\sum_i e_i=1$. Every prime $\mathfrak p$ omits exactly one $e_i$; it contains all the others, hence contains $K_i=\ker(R\to A_i)$. Each $K_i$ is prime since $A_i$ is a domain. Moreover $K_i$ is minimal: if a prime $\mathfrak p\subseteq K_i$ omits $e_j$, then $j=i$ (otherwise $e_i\in\mathfrak p\subseteq K_i$), and so $K_i\subseteq\mathfrak p$. Conversely any minimal prime equals the $K_i$ it contains. Thus [lem-weil-pbc-spec-irreducible-components-minimal-primes] says that the components of $U$ are exactly $V(K_i)$. By the Zariski topology of [def-weil-affine-spectrum], $V(K_i)=D(e_i)$: a prime containing $K_i$ omits $e_i$, and a prime omitting $e_i$ contains $K_i$. They are therefore pairwise disjoint open and closed subsets covering $U$. When $n=0$, $R$ is the zero ring and has no prime ideals, so the same assertion holds for the empty affine open.

source.place: Tag 0357, lemma-normal-locally-finite-nr-irreducibles, affine case; expanded elementary prime/idempotent calculation after algebra.tex Tag 030C

proof.text: For an affine open $U\subseteq Z$, use the order-preserving bijection [lem-weil-pbc-open-subspace-irreducible-closed-correspondence]. If $C$ is a component of $Z$ meeting $U$, then $C\cap U$ is a component of $U$: an irreducible closed set of $U$ containing it would have closure containing $C$, hence equal to $C$ by maximality. Conversely, if $T$ is a component of $U$, its closure in $Z$ is a component of $Z$, because any larger irreducible closed set still meets $U$ and would intersect $U$ in a larger irreducible closed set. Thus the components meeting $U$ correspond exactly to its components, with intersection and closure as inverses.

source.place: Tag 0357, lemma-normal-locally-finite-nr-irreducibles, general case; topology.tex Tag 0B7I, lemma-dimension-supremum-local-dimensions, open-subspace correspondence

proof.text: Fix a component $C$ of $Z$. On every affine open $U$ its intersection is either empty or one of the open components obtained in Step 5, by Step 6. Since affine opens cover a scheme [def-pc-scheme], $C$ is open in $Z$. It is closed by [def-weil-irreducible-components]. Distinct components cannot meet: at a point of intersection choose an affine neighbourhood $U$; their intersections with $U$ are components, hence are disjoint or equal by Step 5, while equality forces equality of their closures by Step 6. Finally every point lies on a component: in an affine neighbourhood it lies on one of the $V(K_i)$ of Step 5, whose closure is a component of $Z$ by Step 6. Together with the global finiteness from Step 2 this proves the finite disjoint open-and-closed decomposition.

Give each component $C$ its open subscheme structure. By [def-weil-open-immersion] its structure sheaf is $\mathcal O_Z|_C$; at $x\in C$ the neighbourhoods contained in $C$ are cofinal among neighbourhoods of $x$ in $Z$, so its stalk equals $\mathcal O_{Z,x}$. Hence $C$ is normal and reduced, the latter by [def-pc-reduced-scheme]. It is nonempty and irreducible by [def-weil-irreducible-components], so the equivalence in [def-pc-integral-scheme] makes it integral. If $Z$ is empty it has no nonempty irreducible subset and hence zero components; all the component assertions are vacuous. This also shows directly why no local Noetherian assumption on the structure sheaf was used.
